$schema: Instance config for an ai-bridge control panel. Customize, then commit. TRACKED, so every value here is a statement both clones of a shared bundle read; the per-machine half lives beside it in the gitignored instance.config.local.json, whose overridable set is listed in ONE place -- SCHEMA.md, 'Per-machine config overrides'. `models` and `roleTiers` below are SEEDED into that local file by /ai-bridge:init and are kept here as the FALLBACK: with neither layer, scripts/resolve-model.sh resolves to nothing and every agent inherits the session model.
$people: EXAMPLE ONLY -- replace both entries below with your team's real GitHub login -> commit email pairs, HERE in this instance. The ai-bridge template is public, so it ships placeholder logins VERIFIED UNCLAIMED on github.com (example-user-007/008 both 404) and addresses at example.com, which RFC 2606 reserves and which cannot receive mail. If you write a new example, verify the login is unclaimed the same way: a plausible name like alice or bob is a real account, and an example naming a stranger is an example someone copies. The address is PER-INSTANCE, not per-person: the same login belongs to a different address in each group's bundle, because the address says which entity the work belongs to -- so never derive it from the login, and never move it into instance.config.local.json (that file says which login this clone IS). Used by scripts/commit-as.sh so each clone authors commits as the human running it; see SCHEMA.md 'Per-machine config overrides'. (/ai-bridge:init offers to collect these when it stamps a NEW bundle at a terminal; it never overwrites what is already here.)
$maxPrLoc: The LINE COUNT past which a PR-opening role agent proposes a split. Absent => 500, which is the number every doc naming this key states, because those docs are read inside bundles whose config predates it -- this seed ships the key PRESENT at 2000, so a freshly stamped bundle uses 2000 and never the fallback. Raise it for fewer, larger PRs (and so fewer external-reviewer sessions); lower it for tighter review units. Never a gate and never a review criterion: the agent SAYS SO in the PR body and opens the PR anyway, because generated boilerplate, codemods and dense logic all move the real number.
$maxPrFiles: The FILE COUNT past which a PR-opening role agent proposes a split, and past which the project-manager proposes splitting a task before dispatch. Absent => 100. It sits beside maxPrLoc because the two count different things and the reviewer counts THIS one: CodeRabbit's free plan refuses a pull request over 100 files outright, before any quota question (measured 2026-09-05, ai-bridge#122 at 147 files), and a `git mv` sweep is 1 file per rename while barely moving the line count. Same status as maxPrLoc in every other respect: the agent SAYS SO and opens the PR anyway, never a gate and never a review criterion.
$maxStallRounds: How many CONSECUTIVE rounds a task may end on the SAME blocker before the PM stops re-dispatching it. Absent => 2, which is the number every doc naming this key states, because those docs are read inside bundles whose config predates it. At the cap the tick runs scripts/stall-counter.sh escalate: status becomes blocked, the blocker is recorded under # Notes, and ONE line goes to AWAITING.md, because the human is this loop's escalation path and a fresh agent at the same wall is not. It is NOT a timeout and not a slow-PR guard: PR activity (a new commit, a new review thread), a changed blocker and a human edit each reset the counter, so only genuine repetition ever reaches the cap. 1 escalates on the first repeat; raise it where an intermittent check is expected to clear itself.
$account: OPTIONAL label naming which Claude account this bundle belongs to, e.g. "proceso". A LABEL, never a credential. Inert on its own: it does anything only while the ai-bridge-accounts companion (from core's own marketplace) is installed, which ships the launcher that starts claude on that account and makes plugin/scripts/resolve-account.sh answer. With both, the welcome banner names the active account and WARNS in red when the session is on a different one and in yellow when it is on none, so a bundle can never quietly run on the other organisation's plan. The account's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR lives under $AI_BRIDGE_ACCOUNTS_HOME (default ~/.claude-accounts) and the launcher refuses one inside a bundle or any git work tree, so no credential can reach this repo.
$board: ON BY DEFAULT, and it is read at BOTH ends of the lifecycle. true (or absent) => /ai-bridge:init creates SNAPSHOT.json when missing on any stamp, so this instance appears on the terminal board, AND each /ai-bridge:dispatch tick re-renders the page to .board-live/board.html (gitignored) and reports that path, AND a tick that actually changed something re-renders the TRACKED /board.html (`build-board.sh --standalone --out board.html .` -- the trailing `.` is load-bearing, it keeps other bundles named by boardInstances out of a file this repo commits) and commits it, which is the whole of how this board is published: repo permissions, no Pages site, nothing account-scoped. false => the snapshot is never created, the installer says so, and the tick renders nothing and says nothing. NOTHING IS SERVED AND NOTHING IS ACCOUNT-SCOPED: the only copy that leaves this machine is the one committed to this repo, so the audience is exactly the repo's permission list and this key costs no data-governance decision beyond who you have already granted access to. A bundle whose board must not be committed at all sets `board: false`, or keeps the `board.html` line in its own .gitignore -- the stamp only ever APPENDS the un-ignore, and git takes the last matching pattern, so a line added after it wins. (The account-scoped publish path, and the config key that recorded its URL, were deleted: only the publishing account could ever update the page, and it vanished from under its own owner at the next login.) Question TEXT still needs SNAPSHOT_QUESTION_TEXT=1 on top of this. scripts/watch-board.sh renders the same file continuously if you want it live between ticks.
$advisor: OPTIONAL read-only tick observer. Add "advisor" to roles to enable it, and set roleTiers.advisor to pick its model (absent => light, the cheapest tier). Omit it and /ai-bridge:dispatch skips that step silently. Its concerns are adjudicated by the deep-tier project-manager before any human sees them, and it has no channel to worker agents, so a cheap model can never steer an expensive one.
$roles: Agents the PM may dispatch as TASK ASSIGNEES. Not every configured agent belongs here — `plan-architect` is deliberately absent: `/plan` and the PM's approach critique dispatch it directly, and no task is ever assigned to it. See `$roleTiers` and SCHEMA.md 'type: Agent'.
$models: Which model alias each TIER costs. PER-MACHINE SPEND, and /ai-bridge:init seeds this key into instance.config.local.json on any stamp that finds it missing there -- so on a stamped instance the LOCAL copy is the one in force and the session banner's FROM column reads `local`. This tracked copy stays as the fallback and as the seed source: removing it would let an unseeded instance resolve to nothing, and an agent that resolves to nothing inherits the session model with no error. Edit the LOCAL file to change what this machine pays; a partial local map overrides entry by entry, and the installer never tops it up. See SCHEMA.md, 'Per-machine config overrides'.
$roleTiers: PER-MACHINE SPEND, seeded and overridden exactly as `models` above (see `$models`). The model tier for ANY agent this instance dispatches, including ones no task is ever assigned to — broader than `roles`. `plan-architect: apex` here and nowhere in `roles` is the intentional case: `models.apex` today affects exactly that one agent, which appears in no `roles` list, so 'what does apex cost me?' is unanswerable from `roles` alone. Do not delete this row to make the two lists match; see SCHEMA.md 'type: Agent' and tests/roles-roletiers-asymmetry.test.sh.
